resources.string: Smart DNS
Open sites that block Iran (Gemini, AI tools, developer services) through a DNS provider that proxies them abroad, while Aether keeps opening filtered sites.
Use Smart DNS
The device resolves names through the servers below instead of 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8. Sites the provider covers see the provider\'s country; everything else keeps the WARP exit.
Only applies to the Aether-only chain. With Psiphon or Tor in front, the exit is already abroad and this setting is ignored.
Protocol
Plain DNS
DNS over HTTPS
DNS over TLS
Classic DNS over UDP (TCP for large answers). Works with every provider, but it is unencrypted.
Queries travel inside HTTPS and look like ordinary web traffic. The most robust choice when the provider offers it.
Queries travel inside TLS on port 853. Encrypted and fast, but port 853 is easier to block.
Smart DNS servers
e.g. https://dns.example.com/dns-query
e.g. dns.example.com
IPv4 addresses, optionally with a port (1.2.3.4:5353), separated by commas, spaces or new lines. Up to 8 servers, tried in order.
HTTPS URLs or host names (the path defaults to /dns-query). Up to 8 servers, tried in order.
Host names or IPv4 addresses, optionally with a port (default 853). Up to 8 servers, tried in order.
None of these is a usable server for the selected protocol. The default resolvers will be used until one is.
Queries go through the tunnel first. If the provider only answers Iranian or registered IPs, Aether switches to reaching it directly by itself, and sends the provider\'s proxies direct too.
Now: through the tunnel.
Now: direct (the provider rejected the tunnel). Proxy ranges detected: %1$d.

Android\'s Private DNS (Settings, Network, Private DNS) must be Off or Automatic, otherwise the system ignores Smart DNS. IPv6 is not offered to apps while Smart DNS is on. Check a site the provider covers, not an IP checker, to confirm it works.
